newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Partco to double size with Dana buy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Partco to double size with Dana buy.

text.p: Fast-growing British auto parts supplier and distributor Partco Group Plc said on Thursday it expected to double its turnover after it acquired the European distribution arm of U.S. components giant Dana Corp.
The 103 million pounds ($168 million) purchase would lift turnover on an annualised basis to 400 million pounds, chief executive Peter Redfern said in an interview.
Such a boost would mean Partco would have more than tripled in size, measured by turnover, since its flotation three years ago when turnover was 124 million pounds

Partco will rely for the purchase on a mixture of its own cash and bank debt, with shareholders being asked to take part in the second rights issue in nine months, this time to raise 69 million pounds at 300p a share.
Last year shareholders were asked for 42.5 million of the 56 million pound purchase price of Serck Marston, a cooling radiator distributor bought from BTR Plc and IMI Plc.
News of the Dana deal, and the rights issue details, barely dented Partco's share price on an otherwise flat London stock market and the shares eased five pence to 351.5 by 1315 GMT.
Redfern said the proposed buy would lift his company's leading share of the British independent-supplier auto parts market to 13 percent from its current level of 8.0 percent.
"It will get materially earnings enhancing in 1998 (and) there are lots of synergies," he added.
One of the key elements in the Dana Distribution Europe business is a chain of paint products stores across Britain called Brown Brothers, which has 135 distribution points.
"Brown Brothers fits superbly into the Partco Group and the acquisition is based on very strong industrial logic," Redfern said, noting Browns brought with it a market-leading presence.
Other attractive European operations include a strong business in the Netherlands which, in combination with Partco's existing Belgian distribution company, should be a strong base.
"We see the opportunity for getting more horsepower from Benelux is obviously appreciable," he told Reuters.
Even with an increased British market share, and a platform for further organic growth, Redfern said: "There is a lot of growth to go for in the UK."
The company expects the deal will need only 1.5 million pounds in extraordinary costs this year, he added, saying the deal aimed to catalyse growth, not to shrink or rationalise any businesses.
From a financial point of view, the planned acquisition will have a minor impact on Partco's gearing, lifting it to about 107 percent by the end of this year from just above 100 percent at present.
More importantly, Redfern argued, the company's cash-to- interest cover would remain well over six times.
The chief executive said he was confident the incoming units would be as cash-generative as Partco's existing business and that the cycle of funding more bolt-on growth from cash could go on.
"That's what it boils down to -- we tend to use our cash to reinvest in the business and grow it," he said. "There's no reason at all to stop".
"What we've got to do is carry through this acquisition and get down to integrating the businesses so we've got a damn good springboard for the next one," Redfern said. ($1=.6109 Pound)
